scenes.narration: The key to room 14 was warm when the night clerk handed it to me, like someone had been holding it all evening.
The motel sat alone off the highway, nine rooms, one flickering sign, and a parking lot with exactly one other car.
Inside, the bed was made, but the pillow had a dent in it, and the bathroom mirror was still fogged from a shower.
I called the front desk. The clerk said nobody had stayed in 14 for three weeks, not since the man who never checked out.
At two in the morning, the other car started outside, drove one slow circle around the lot, and parked again.
Then the knock came, three soft taps, and through the peephole I saw the clerk, holding a second warm key.
He whispered that the man who never checked out always comes back for his room, and tonight he had brought him the key.
I left through the bathroom window, and when I looked back, the light in room 14 was on and the dent in the pillow was gone.
